title: Energy-Efficient Multi-Operand XOR Logic-Based CIM Accelerator using RRAM technology
problem: Compute-in-memory (CIM) accelerators with standard RRAM suffer from energy overhead in multi-operand operations; XOR-based logic-in-memory can reduce switching activity but requires efficient circuit design.
motivation: RRAM-based CIM with XOR logic reduces energy per operation for sparse neural networks and graph algorithms; logic in RRAM memory eliminates data movement overhead.
method: Design RRAM-based CIM array with XOR-logic operators embedded in crossbar periphery. Use voltage-to-time converter for multi-operand computation; optimize timing and voltage margins for energy efficiency while maintaining accuracy.
key_novelty: RRAM CIM accelerator leveraging XOR logic operators with voltage-to-time conversion for multi-operand computation.
contributions: RRAM crossbar design with embedded XOR logic operators
Energy-efficiency analysis for sparse neural networks
Demonstrated improvements over standard RRAM CIM
limitations: Analysis limited to abstract; specific sparse network benchmarks and energy measurements not detailed.
primary_theme: RRAM CIM with XOR logic-based multi-operand computation
